remove: From morning till evening he works.
He works from morning to evening.
From morning to evening he works.
why: Three renderings of a different sentence entirely — «Он рабо́тает с утра́ до ве́чера», not «Он дожда́лся у́тра до́ма». They read as a block left behind when the Russian they were written for was replaced. Present since before the review; harmless while the word bank built its tiles from the primary alone, but assemblable — and so reliably offered as a correct answer — once the bank was widened to make curated alternates usable.

The proposal's own note says «бо́жьи созда́ния» is the set phrase "God's creatures" and that "divine creatures" claims they are themselves godlike — something the Russian does not say. An accepted answer has to be an equally valid translation, not the wording the review just rejected.

remove: She took offence at my brother.
why: Changes the referent: with a third-person subject and no possessive, «на бра́та» is the subject's own brother, so "my brother" names a different person.

remove: He told us about his childhood.
why: Invents an addressee — the Russian has no «нам». The proposal was an over-translation fix and then re-accepted the over-translation.

remove: There was not enough on the stamp for the letter.
why: Invents a postage value the Russian never mentions, and is not idiomatic English; «ма́рки не хвати́ло» is simply that the stamp did not suffice.

remove: The Ukrainian told us about his city.
why: Invents an addressee — the same defect the proposal was fixing.
